hypothesis: Declaring the existing builder host as the task-staging owner and deferring only protected Git index denials will let native agents execute canonical task transitions without granting Git metadata writes or weakening rollback for transient and undeclared staging failures.

metricsCompared.name: canonical native task transition
metricsCompared.baseline: The live source-mode task CLI reached git add but failed with an Operation not permitted index.lock error and rolled the ready-to-doing transition back.
metricsCompared.candidate: The same live CLI completed ready-to-doing under the declared workflow-host owner while the linked-worktree Git index remained protected for the agent.

metricsCompared.name: deferred-staging and rollback regression coverage
metricsCompared.baseline: The host retry had coverage only for a manually moved task file and did not cover the canonical mover's protected-index path.
metricsCompared.candidate: 54 of 54 focused repo-task, CLI, runtime-resource, claimed-task staging, module-dependency, strict-type policy, and root-layout tests pass, including protected denial deferral plus undeclared and transient denial rejection.

metricsCompared.name: review-window failure-cluster disposition
metricsCompared.baseline: The source progress review reported eight open dead letters and recurring native-harness failure signatures.
metricsCompared.candidate: The operator capture records 8 of 8 canonical dispositions with rationale, three successful later builder runs, and a later progress review with zero open dead letters and no cited native-harness signatures.

rationale: The candidate uses the already-required claim-scoped host staging repair and grants no new Git write root. Deferral requires both the builder-owned runtime declaration and the specific protected index.lock permission signature; transient locks, undeclared callers, and every other staging failure retain rollback. Focused runtime, protocol, architecture, type, build, formatting, and workflow validation pass.
